gen-dafont-alien-encounters-fs-trench-sl: Big gaps between its letter pairs give Alien Encounters a drifting, otherworldly look. Trench Slab is the classic serif counterpart, dignified and tightly set, with caps that barely rise above the lowercase.
gen-dafont-arkhip-fs-sentient: Arkhip floats its letters well apart, with a bent-paperclip c and no thickening or thinning anywhere. Sentient tucks its apertures in tight and lets curves thin out slightly, which gives the pair its sharpest tension: open against closed.
gen-dafont-azonix-fs-bespoke-slab: Wide, wiry and a bit stubborn. Azonix draws crisp, wide-mouthed capitals that hold up when shrunk, while Bespoke Slab, a text serif with tall lowercase bodies, handles the quieter, grounded work.
gen-dafont-azonix-fs-trench-slab: Azonix bends its strokes like cable, with no swelling or thinning, and its capitals barely clear the lowercase. And Trench Slab, a text serif with the same low step up to its caps, would read steadily and sturdily over a long passage.
gen-dafont-blockletter-fs-bespoke-slab: Blockletter's tall midsection looks sketched by a pencil that never presses harder. Bespoke Slab, a serif with tall lowercase bodies, would carry a long passage in a grounded, steady way.
gen-dafont-blockletter-fs-erode: Erode opens this pair with a tall middle band and shallow ascenders. Over a long passage its gentle ebb and flow of stroke weight stays inviting, while Blockletter holds a marker-like line up top.
gen-dafont-bloody-fs-bespoke-slab: Big round lowercase bowls make Bloody look heavy and commanding. Bespoke Slab sits beneath it with tall, grounded lowercase, so the heading shouts once and the text keeps talking quietly.
gen-dafont-bloody-fs-erode: Round, loud and unmistakably bloody. Erode, a serif with a gentle ebb and flow of stroke weight, handles the sustained reading, leaving Bloody to its low-contrast bowls and big statements.
gen-dafont-bloody-fs-hoover: Hoover is a serif with a generous entry into the e and compressed ascenders. Under Bloody's big round bowls it settles into a tidy, robust text block that lets the heading dominate.
gen-dafont-bloody-fs-trench-slab: Trench Slab keeps its caps close to the lowercase height, which gives the text a dignified, compact look. And Bloody, with its big round bowls, earns its place when set large and short.
